vibe.rationale: Vibe 5 — one-point upgrade from July 12's Vibe 4. Two positive resolutions defined the July 12-13 interreporting cycle and both were explicitly identified in the July 12 brief as the conditions required for a Vibe 5 re-upgrade. First: Chelan Hills Fire 100% contained with all evacuations lifted. The July 12 brief characterized 'Chelan Hills Level 3 downgrade confirmation' as a primary watchitem and noted that 95% containment was expected to complete to full containment on Day 8. The confirmation arrived on July 13 — full containment, all evacuations lifted, demobilization complete. This completes the full arc from July 4 ignition through July 13 resolution: 9 days, 9,861 acres, 19 primary residences destroyed, $9.1M+ preliminary damage, 1 fatality. Second: Measles June 19 Lumen Field primary incubation window resolved. July 12 was Day 10 (the sub-window's final day), and the July 12 brief carried forward the 'if July 12 Georgetown wastewater close is clean, the brief will characterize the June 19 cluster risk as resolved for the primary incubation window in the July 13 morning session' forward commitment. That characterization is now operative: three-day consecutive clean streak July 10-11-12 through the Days 8-9-10 peak window is the strongest epidemiological reassurance sequence of the 2026 arc. These two positive resolutions — fire and public health — were explicitly the Vibe 4 ceiling breakers identified in the July 12 brief, and both arrived. The dominant negative — Hormuz MOU Acute Stress Day 6 — has not further deteriorated in the July 13 cycle. No fourth kinetic exchange confirmed through Monday evening. The three MOU termination-instrument absences (SNSC formal void declaration / CENTCOM naval blockade reinstatement / Kharg Island strike) remain intact through Day 25, maintaining the MOU's legal operative status. WTI stabilizing near $73-74 — the Saturday night re-escalation premium is not spiking further on July 13, which is the cautiously positive oil signal consistent with a Vibe 5 rather than Vibe 3. The June CPI T-1 setup (Cleveland Fed nowcast ~3.8% YoY, down from 4.2% May) is the session's most consequential forward signal: a sub-4.0% June print would be the first deflationary CPI momentum signal since July 7 and would materially support Warsh's September SEP deflationary thesis. Negative factor 1 (Hormuz Acute Stress Day 6): THREE CONSECUTIVE US STRIKE EXCHANGES IN FIVE DAYS — the most kinetically active MOU period; diplomatic channel status ambiguous after simultaneous July 11 talks-and-strikes; no confirmed nuclear technical timeline session from resumed July 11 talks; WTI above normalization floor ($74); Lloyd's normalization blocked pending contested compliance resolution. Negative factor 2 (Russia Omsk Day 13): 75% offline, multi-month restoration, diesel export ban through July, Central Asian spillover, Warsh September dual-shock thesis constrained. Negative factor 3 (B and O Fire Day 4): Okanogan terrain onset region Day 16 — not yet large fire (cautiously positive) but structural rapid-escalation risk identical to Kartar Fire suppression-challenge arc; east-wind season active. Positive factor 1 (Chelan Hills 100%): DECISIVE RESOLUTION — 100% containment confirmed, all evacuations lifted; $25K reward offered; recovery arc commencing for McNeil Canyon; BPA demand relief confirmed. Positive factor 2 (Measles window resolved): PRIMARY CLUSTER RISK RESOLVED for June 19 Lumen Field mass event; three-day peak-window clean streak July 10-11-12 confirmed; Seafair Fleet Week (July 21-24) next major Seattle mass-attendance event. Positive factor 3 (June CPI T-1): Expected 3.8% YoY — if confirmed tomorrow, first sub-4.0% CPI since tariff and Hormuz shock compounded; operative input for Warsh September FOMC; energy component deceleration thesis requires WTI to cooperate below $72 (not yet achieved but directionally favorable). Positive factor 4 (Peru Fujimori credentials T-1): JNE ceremony tomorrow July 15; Milei attending; smooth transition continuing; inauguration July 28 on track. Upgrade to Vibe 6 requires: June CPI confirms at or below 3.8%; US-Iran diplomatic channel confirmed operative with nuclear technical timeline session scheduled; WTI declines below $72 and holds; B and O Fire confirmed contained or insignificant acreage; Lloyd's war-risk normalization announcement. Drop to Vibe 4 requires: Fourth US-Iran kinetic exchange July 13-14 with no diplomatic output; WTI spiking above $76 on fourth exchange signal; B and O Fire rapid escalation to large-fire scale under east-wind onset conditions; June CPI upside surprise above 4.5%; SNSC void declaration issued.

items.summary: The July 13 session marks MOU Day 25 and Acute Stress Day 6 — defined by the absence of a fourth kinetic exchange rather than by any confirmed positive diplomatic development. The dominant analytical structure from the July 12 brief carries forward with a cautiously stabilizing oil signal: WTI settled near $73-74 on Monday rather than spiking above $75 on the Saturday night exchange, which is the minimum positive signal required to prevent a further Vibe downgrade. The three MOU termination-instrument absences remain intact: no SNSC formal void declaration, no CENTCOM naval blockade reinstatement, no Kharg Island strike. Iran's Supreme National Security Council has not formally declared the MOU null and void. The MOU's legal operative status through Day 25 is the structural reality — the MOU is under acute stress, not terminated. The operative unknown is the July 11 Qatar/Pakistan communication channel. The resumed talks on July 11 daytime (confirmed Al Arabiya / Times of Israel) preceded Saturday night's third exchange by hours. Whether those talks produced any deliverable — a nuclear technical timeline proposal, a cooling-off message, a cessation-of-kinetic-exchange commitment — is unconfirmed in the July 13 reporting cycle. If the channel produced output that is being evaluated by Iranian and American principals, the July 13 absence of a fourth exchange is consistent with a managed pause rather than a conflict escalation spiral. If the channel produced no output, the July 13 absence of a fourth exchange is either fortuitous or reflects the logistical tempo of the US strike planning cycle rather than any diplomatic achievement. The brief cannot assign probability to either interpretation without confirmed channel output reporting. Iran's new Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei — installed March 8 by the Assembly of Experts following the February 28 Israeli assassination of Ayatollah Ali Khamenei — remains in hiding, communicating only through written statements. His six-day public funeral was held in early July. The US Defense Department assessed in March that Mojtaba was 'wounded and likely disfigured' in the same strikes that killed his father; Reuters reported in April a potential leg amputation. An incapacitated supreme leader communicating via written statements, without a visible face or voice, is the structural factor that makes every Iranian negotiating signal ambiguous at the principal level: the July 11 resumed talks involved Iranian officials but not a supreme leader who can be publicly verified as operative. This is the Iran succession uncertainty that has complicated the MOU from Day 1. June CPI releases tomorrow (Tuesday July 14, 8:30 AM ET). Cleveland Fed nowcast: approximately 3.8% year-over-year, down from 4.2% in May. A sub-4.0% confirmation would be the first deflationary CPI momentum signal since the May print and would materially support Warsh's September FOMC deflationary thesis — if WTI simultaneously holds below $74 through August. The July 14 CPI print is the most consequential single data release for the brief's economic arc since the May CPI on June 10.

items.summary: Six secondary geopolitical threads on July 13 evening. First: FIFA World Cup 2026 semifinals are confirmed. France vs. Spain plays Tuesday July 14 at AT&T Stadium in Arlington, Texas. England vs. Argentina plays Wednesday July 15. The Argentina-Switzerland quarterfinal was won on Julian Alvarez's long-range strike in the 112th minute. The dual semifinal window (July 14-15) coincides with the Peru JNE credentials ceremony (July 15) and the June CPI release (July 14) — a dense geopolitical-economic-sports convergence window. The World Cup continues to run in the NIFC-FIFA co-response context: NIFC PL4 at Day 15, mass venue co-response posture active for semifinal venues. Second: Russia fuel crisis Day 13. Omsk refinery remains 75% offline (CDU-10 destroyed / CDU-11 infrastructure damage). No restoration progress signals through Day 13. Russia's diesel export ban through end of July maintains Central Asian supply spillover: Uzbekistan flight cuts active; Kazakhstan China-import insurance continuing. The IEA 'unprecedented' dual-shock designation stands. Warsh's September FOMC deflationary thesis now requires three concurrent favorable signals — Hormuz normalization, Russian refining recovery, and commodity price relief — none of which are in progress. Third: Lebanon fragile hold Day 28. The 48-hour post-third-exchange window (July 11-13) has closed without any confirmed Iranian operational direction to Hezbollah. No Hezbollah mobilization orders through July 13 evening. Iran's post-Khamenei chain of command — Mojtaba Khamenei in hiding, communicating through written statements — creates genuine uncertainty about whether Lebanon escalation orders can be issued and verified in a timely manner. The July 13 Lebanon clean assessment is cautiously positive but structurally uncertain. Fourth: Peru — JNE credentials ceremony tomorrow (July 15, Gran Teatro Nacional, San Borja, noon). First Vice President Galarreta and Second Vice President Torres co-credentialed. Argentine President Milei confirmed attendance. Keiko Fujimori won by 49,641 votes in the full official count (June 30); JNE formally declared her president-elect July 3. Inauguration July 28. Resource nationalism premium in copper and silver markets at lower-risk level. Fifth: Colombia — de la Espriella inauguration T-25 (August 7). Transition continuing without complications. New government inherits Venezuela earthquake humanitarian burden Day 1. Sixth: Venezuela earthquake Day 20. 1,719+ confirmed dead, 46,600+ missing. Maduro continues restricting US humanitarian access. Colombia's incoming government will inherit the most acute Venezuela-border humanitarian scenario since the Uribe era. Seventh: Congo Ebola — new suspected cases reported beyond the Ituri epicenter, signaling geographic spread of the current outbreak. Not yet at the threshold of a regional WHO Public Health Emergency declaration but under active monitoring.

items.summary: The July 13 economic session is defined by the countdown to the June CPI release (Tuesday July 14, 8:30 AM ET) — the most consequential economic data point for the Warsh September FOMC deflationary thesis since the May CPI print. Cleveland Fed inflation nowcast: approximately 3.8% year-over-year for June CPI (all items), down from 4.2% in May. A sub-4.0% print would be the first deflationary CPI momentum signal since May and would represent the energy and supply-shock deceleration that Warsh's inaugural June 17 press conference cited as the prerequisite for a September rate hold rather than hike. The Kiplinger June CPI preview characterizes the setup as 'don't let a negative headline fool you' — acknowledging that energy price base effects from the Hormuz arc may produce a headline deceleration that overstates underlying disinflation if core components remain sticky. The WTI stabilization near $73-74 on Monday is the optimal setup condition for a favorable June energy CPI component: if oil stayed elevated through the June measurement period, the base effects could be unfavorable; but the sub-$72 normalization zone that WTI briefly touched on July 11 (before Saturday night's third exchange pushed it back to $73-74) suggests the June energy average was below the worst-case July 7+ re-escalation levels. The 61% September rate hike probability (CME FedWatch) is the operative market bet that Warsh moves rather than holds — the June CPI is the most important single data input that could shift that probability in either direction. A June CPI print at 3.8% YoY would exert downward pressure on the September hike probability toward 40-45%; a June CPI above 4.5% would push it above 70%. The dual inflationary shock — Hormuz re-escalation premium sustaining WTI above $72 and Russia Omsk 75% offline extending natural gas/fuel feedstock disruption — is the structural constraint on Warsh's deflationary thesis. Both required favorable conditions for a September SEP rate hold (Hormuz normalization producing WTI below $72 through August; Russian refining recovery reducing fertilizer and industrial gas inputs) are operationally constrained: Hormuz at Acute Stress Day 6 prevents WTI below $72; Omsk recovery is multi-month. The June CPI tomorrow is a data-point input, not a structural resolution. Equity market conditions entering the CPI: the Schwab Monday characterization ('Market on Edge Watching Strait as Chip Firm Debuts') from July 12 has evolved to a cautious Monday open, with the Dow in the ~53,000-53,200 range, S&P near 7,480-7,520, constrained by Strait uncertainty but partially supported by the June CPI favorable setup. The July 14 print is the single most important watch event across all brief domains for the July 13-14 window.

items.summary: Five secondary economic-legislative threads on July 13 evening. First: Tariff calendar convergence. Section 122 expires July 24 (T-11). USTR Section 301 completion deadline July 20 (T-7). No White House finalization of Section 301 successor framework announced through July 13 evening. The 3-4 day gap between Section 301 completion (July 20) and Section 122 expiry (July 24) remains the operative importer planning risk window. The proposed Section 301 architecture (12.5% on 46 countries primary; 10% on 15 others including EU/Canada/UK/Mexico, with no rate cap and no time limit) represents a materially different long-term tariff posture than Section 122's 15%-capped, 150-day structure. Any White House finalization announcement in the July 13-20 window provides the material clarity event for importers navigating the structural tariff transition. Pharma 232 effective July 31 (T-18). Second: FERC AI 30-day informational report T-5 (July 18). Six ISO/RTO operators (PJM/MISO/SPP/CAISO/ISO-NE/NYISO) in final week of submissions on large energy user grid connection tariff rules. Any early submission by a major operator ahead of July 18 would be the first formal statement of national large-load integration position. PNW Climate Week Day 1 (opening today July 13) directly precedes and politically frames the July 18 submissions — AI data center electricity demand governance is a central dual-mandate topic at the week-long forum. Third: OBBB Law Day 14 (signed June 29, effective July 1). Medicaid work requirements and SNAP restrictions in 18 states. Zero federal court stays on any OBBB title. CBO 10-year deficit estimate: $3.4 trillion. The Aragon v. Rollins downstream legal exposure accumulates through Day 14. No new OBBB legal or procedural developments July 13. Susan Collins in November 2026 (T-14). No replacement candidate confirmed publicly. The nominee-selection process is the brief's most underappreciated near-term political calendar item — a well-resourced Democratic challenger in a Collins competitive-state race is a material midterm cycle factor.

items.summary: The July 13 Washington fire session records the decisive resolution of the 2026 fire season's most consequential WUI event. The Chelan Hills Fire is 100% contained as of the July 12-13 cycle. All evacuation orders have been lifted. Douglas County Sheriff Tyler Caille confirmed the full containment milestone, announced a $25,000 reward to identify the human-caused ignition responsible for the fire, and described the investigation as active with county and state investigators working in parallel. The final confirmed damage picture: 19 primary residences total loss (revised down from the July 12 brief's '100+ structures' characterization — the larger structure count reflected all structures including secondary, outbuildings, and auxiliary; primary residences total loss is 19), 6 additional residences damaged, 1 fatality, $9.1M+ preliminary damage estimate. The Chelan Hills Fire ignited July 4 near Orondo, Douglas County, on US-97 at approximately MP-233. Its nine-day arc — 0% to 100% containment on 9,861 acres with the WUI emergency posture throughout — was the brief's most resource-intensive single event of the 2026 Washington fire season. The full containment with evacuations lifted enables BPA to fully release the demand management associated with the WUI fire-proximity east-of-Cascades tie line configuration. McNeil Canyon begins the long recovery arc: FEMA Region 10 declarations, long-term recovery assistance, contractor coordination, and Douglas County property damage assessment are the downstream processes. The B and O Fire (Day 4, near Okanogan WA, July 9 ignition) remains the brief's highest-priority unresolved PNW fire thread for July 13. The key July 13 data point: the fire is still not confirmed at large-fire scale at Day 4. Four-plus days since ignition without large-fire confirmation (no ICS-209 designation) is a cautiously positive suppression signal — the initial attack response appears to be containing the fire's growth.
